Baseline score

6.7 out of 10

You give AI concrete inputs and steer the work through follow-ups. Explicit verification has the most room to improve.

How it’s scored. Across 18 chats, each habit earns its weight multiplied by its share of chats. Concrete inputs carry 4 points (15/18), follow-ups 3 (14/18), and explicit verification 3 (6/18). The sum rounds to 6.7.

    Prompt library

    Ground the first ask

    Name the output and point to one source. Ask AI to flag gaps in the evidence.

    Make one precise revision

    Say what to change, what to keep, and what to check again.

    Set a passing check

    Ask for a specific result, such as a form that submits on mobile. For consequential work, name the step that needs your approval.

    Sample and scoring method

    I selected nine work chats each from accessible ChatGPT and Codex history. Codex examples cluster around one technical project. The sample is purposive and two Codex chats are represented by their latest ten turns. Counts cover visible user messages, including submitted choices, and behaviors are coded once per chat. Iteration counts any chat with two or more user messages.

    Claude coverage comes from handoffs discussed in the sampled chats. Direct Claude conversations and outcomes were outside the available sample. The review uses aggregate counts and paraphrased work patterns.
